bull.b: Consistent, large free cash flow that roughly equals net income and has grown ~25% provides durable funding for dividends, debt reduction and accretive investments. This cash-backed earnings quality reduces reliance on capital markets and supports multi-quarter execution of growth plans.

bull.t: Operational momentum: same-store NOI and occupancy
bull.b: Double-digit same-store NOI growth with stronger RevPOR and significant occupancy gains indicates durable demand and better per-unit economics. Sustained flow-through and margin expansion from these drivers support recurring FFO growth over the next several quarters if operational improvements persist.

bull.t: Balance sheet liquidity and capital access
bull.b: Healthy cash on hand, manageable leverage near ~3x, and demonstrated access to capital (senior notes, positive agency outlooks) give the company flexibility to fund acquisitions, repay maturing debt and support dividends over multiple quarters without forcing distressed asset sales.

bear.t: Execution risk on lower-occupied SHOP assets
bear.b: A sizable portion of SHOP NOI comes from recently acquired, lower-occupancy assets that require meaningful lease-up and operational improvement. If WBS-driven lift and occupancy recovery are slower than planned, expected cash flow conversion and targeted returns may lag for multiple quarters, pressuring FFO per share.

bear.t: Potential equity dilution from capital recycling
bear.b: A large ATM program plus active disposition and reinvestment activity increases the probability of equity issuance to fund acquisitions. While flexible, ongoing issuance could dilute FFO/share and slow per-share growth if new investments or lease-ups take time to generate targeted cash returns.

bear.t: Development returns and structural labor pressure
bear.b: Elevated construction costs and noted structural labor availability concerns constrain development economics and raise operating expense risk. These input pressures can compress future project yields and increase ExpPOR over time, limiting margin expansion and the pace of accretive organic growth.
